correctness.rationale: Diagonalizing the SPD Hessian reduces the published iteration exactly to \(u_{k+1}=(1+m-s)u_k-mu_{k-1}\), with \(m=\alpha-\theta\lambda\) and \(s=\beta\lambda\). The necessary-and-sufficient quadratic Jury conditions give \(-1<m<1\) and \(0<s<2(1+m)\). For \(0\le\alpha<1\), requiring this over all \(\lambda\in[\mu,L]\) reduces exactly to \(L(\beta+2\theta)<2(1+\alpha)\). Root-product and discriminant arguments prove the complete modewise rate optimum, including the one-update cancellation at \(m=0,s=1\). The packaged checker independently reconstructs these identities and characteristic-root spot checks.

value.rationale: The primary method introduces Hessian correction as an acceleration mechanism, so understanding what that parameter does on the canonical SPD model is a natural design question. The finding gives a complete answer: correction subtracts curvature times \(\theta\) from momentum, can exactly cancel inertia at a selected curvature, and consumes twice its coefficient in the sharp global stability budget. The one-update isotropic case and the full modewise rate law are structural parameter-design facts, not arbitrary finite computations, and they explain both the potential benefit and the stability cost of Hessian-driven damping.
